title: Tanya Chaudhary Smashes National Hammer Throw Record Days Before Asian Games
excerpt: The Uttar Pradesh athlete sent the hammer to 68.35m at the Indian Athletics Series Final on Thursday, breaking 18-year-old Anushka Yadav's record with the Aichi-Nagoya Games beginning September 19.
body:
• Tanya Chaudhary hurled the hammer 68.35 metres at the Indian Athletics Series Final on Thursday, breaking the national record by a massive 1.33 metres.
  • The previous record of 67.02m belonged to 18-year-old Anushka Yadav, set in June 2026 in Bhubaneswar; she finished second with 66.34m.
  • Both Uttar Pradesh athletes are in India's Asian Games squad, with the Aichi-Nagoya Games beginning on September 19.
  • The new mark is more than four metres beyond the bronze-medal throw at the last Asian Games in Hangzhou.

Record falls days before the Asian Games

NEW DELHI: Indian athletics received a timely boost days before the Asian Games as Uttar Pradesh's Tanya Chaudhary shattered the women's hammer throw national record at the Indian Athletics Series Final on Thursday. Chaudhary sent the hammer to 68.35 metres, bettering her state-mate Anushka Yadav's record of 67.02m — set only in June — by a staggering 1.33 metres.

Yadav, the 18-year-old who had held the record since the National Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar, finished second with a best effort of 66.34m — itself a throw beyond her own previous record. Chaudhary pocketed Rs 1 lakh for the victory, while Yadav received Rs 50,000 for second place.

Both athletes are part of India's Asian Games squad, making the record-breaking performance particularly significant with the Games beginning on September 19 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.

Context & Background

The women's hammer throw has become India's fastest-improving field event. The national record stood at 65.25m, set by Sarita Singh in 2017, for nine years. Yadav broke it in June with her 67.02m, clearing the Asian Games qualifying mark of 61.72m along the way. Now, less than three months later, Chaudhary has raised the bar again.

Chaudhary's previous official personal best was 63.91m, recorded in August 2025. She did throw 65.60m at the Inter-University Championships in January 2026, but that mark could not be ratified because the meet is not a World Athletics-recognised event and she was not subjected to a dope test afterwards. Thursday's throw removes all doubt — it came in an official competition and rewrites the record books properly.

The 22-year-old finished seventh at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou with a best of 60.50m, and her improvement since is striking: she is now throwing nearly eight metres farther than she did three years ago.

Impact & Analysis

Context matters. At the Hangzhou Asian Games, the women's hammer throw bronze medal went to South Korea's Kim Tae-hui with 64.14m. Chaudhary's 68.35m is more than four metres beyond that, and Yadav's 66.34m on the same day would also have challenged for a podium place. India could conceivably send two athletes to the circle in Japan capable of standing on the medal stand.

The Athletics Federation of India initially named a 77-member athletics squad for the Games, since expanded to 79 athletes, and India's overall contingent stands at 503 athletes across 36 sports. The athletics team will compete without injured javelin star Neeraj Chopra, and the rise of the field events — from Dev Kumar Meena's pole vault records to the hammer throw duels — has become one of the bright spots of the build-up.

What's Next

The hammer throw at the Asian Games now shapes up as one of the most anticipated events for India. Chaudhary and Yadav will likely trade throws at the top of the standings — a rivalry that has already produced two national records this season. The Aichi-Nagoya Games open on September 19, and the hammer throw circle will be one of the events India watches most closely.
